text_fidelity_a:
Allen 102S Premium 2-Bike Trunk Mount Rack I placed this bike rack onto my 2003 Nissan Sentra. I knew this was the correct rack to buy thanks to the website that provides a list (Visit the fit list FIRST before purchasing an Allen bike rack): [...]

Anyway, since this bike rack had such good reviews and it was the right one for my car, I decided to buy it. Hooking it up was fairly easy. I'll admit, I struggled a little bit only because it was my fist attempt, but I know that it will be a peace of cake from now on. Once you get it right the first time, the future attempts will be perfectly easy. When I was finished, I put my body weight onto it to ensure it was sturdy enough for a bike, and it was definitely safe! That bike rack was not going to go anywhere! The straps and everything ensured it was sturdy and safe for the road!

I had to pick up my new bike today (A Schwinn Riverside 26" female bike that looks like this: [...]. As you can tell by the photo, my bike is a female bike. Because it is a female bike WITHOUT a straight bar, I had to purchase a second part that is also by Allen seen here: http://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B000ELSSZE/ref=oh_details_o00_s00_i00. This bar is easy to install as well. It took me about ten seconds to place it onto my bike securely. This allowed me to easily put my bike onto the rack without any issues. Keep in mind, this is only for bikes that do NOT have a straight bar. You may or may not need this part. I needed it for mine.

Once I placed the bike onto the rack, I tightened up the straps. One thing I noticed is that the front wheel of the bike was not secure. It was free to turn as I drove, which would bang into my car, so I simply got a bungee cord and wrapped it in a way to prevent it from moving while I drove. I also got a bungee cord for the back wheel to prevent that wheel from spinning (this is not necessary, but I just prefer to do this). The peddles of the bike hit the bumper, so I would also recommend socks or clothes of some sort to be wrapped around them so they don't scratch the paint of your car.

Anyway, my bike and I made it home perfectly fine. The bike was very secure and sturdy on the bike rack. That bike was not going anywhere, even though I went up and down hills and made a lot of turns on my way home at around 50mph. I have not gone on the highway with it yet, but based on my experience so far, I am certain it is fine.

Overall, I recommend this product! It's great!
text_fidelity_b: Allen 102S Premium 2-Bike Trunk Mount Rack

text_fidelity_a:
Camp Chef Rainier Grill and Portable Camp Stove When I purchased the unit I thought it came with the griddle too. It doesn't. I thought I'd be able to buy the griddle separately but it was readily apparent it was not available from Camp Chef or anywhere else. I thought about returning the unit because the aluminum grill material will not hold a pot or a griddle without being damaged. If you are looking to buy the stove make sure you get the Camp Chef Ranier Combo which includes the griddle. For some reason though the Combo stove is 40% more expensive than the base Ranier Grill Camp stove. It is for that reason I passed on returning what I had purchased and looked for a cheaper jury-rigged solution.

We solved the grill limitations by purchasing a $12 BBQ rectangle expansion grate from a local hardware warehouse. I removed the expansion arms and cut off two of the grates from one end with an angle grinder, but left the grate supports so the gratefree end had about a 2" extension on each side. The extensions fit nicely under the single burner grate and the adapted grill perfectly covered the grilling section of the stove. The adapted grate moves a little, but very little. We can use the grill section now for a griddle we already own or an additional pot. You cannot use the adapted grill for grilling though because the gas burner element in the grilling section is not protected from fat drippings. When we want to grill, we just remove the adapted grill and replace it with the original grill that came with the stove because it has the burner element protector built down the center of the grill.

Now, having said all that, we love the stove. We use it with the bulk hose adapter for a 20 lb propane bottle. The single burner quickly boils water and is relatively adjustable for pot/pan cooking. The stove burners light with one or two clicks of the lighter button. If all I wanted was the grill and stove I would have given it 5 stars, but the fact that the combo unit is so much more expensive and the griddle is not available as a separate purchase, resulting in a jury-rig solution, I gave it four stars
text_fidelity_b: Camp Chef Rainier Grill and Portable Camp Stove

text_fidelity_a:
YAKIMA, ForkLift Fork Mount Bike Carrier for Roof Racks, 1 Bike Capacity I bought one of these racks in June 2017 from REI, and have used it many times over the year. The rack is a good solution for my Mazda 5 roof bars, though it's somewhat challenging to get my fairly heavy Electra Townie on and off the car (I'm not a strong person).

I bought a second rack recently (December 2017). The new rack has a different "skewer" design than the old one. The old skewer had a "cap" on one end, and the locking/folding head screws on and off. The new skewer has the locking/folding head fixed to the bolt, and the cap on the opposite side screws on and off. My problem with the new design is that it's simply not as secure as the old one. With a lock core fitted and locked, the old locking head simply cannot be removed when a bike is clamped in (well, it could be by somebody with a hacksaw or something, but it's at least conceptually a sound system). Because the new skewer has a screw-off cap opposite the locking end, the lock is irrelevant: the screw can simply be removed and the bike is free.

The attached photo shows the old skewer ("A" and "B" for the locking head and the fixed end cap), and the new skewer ("C" for the locking head and "D" is the screw-off endcap).

Update: I heard back from Yakima support. Apparently there's a mechanism in the new endcap on the skewer that does pretty much what the spring-loaded sleeve on the old locking mechanism did. When the cap is tight against the fork, it actually cannot be removed at all easily. So two stars back :)
text_fidelity_b: YAKIMA, ForkLift Fork Mount Bike Carrier for Roof Racks, 1 Bike Capacity

text_fidelity_a:
Isokinetics Inc. Brand Adjustable Fitness Ball Chair - Metal Frame - 2 Frame Finishes - Exclusive: 60mm (2.5") Wheels - Multiple Ball Color Choices - Adjustable Base and Back Height I get so many compliments on this chair! And I love it!

It is constructed very well. It supports my weight well (230 pounds...working on getting that down) and glides easily. I spent some time not realizing that the ball was not completely inflated, probably in fear that it would explode if I pumped too much more. Definitely follow the instructions for blowing it up - you have to let it sit for the night without 100% capacity - so don't buy this with the intention of using it the same day (this is true of any chair like this!) Don't skip that part! Then, when you finally do blow it up all the way, know that in a month or so you may want to blow it up further. When I refilled it, the ball didn't touch the group (even despite my weight!) and it changed where the back bolster hit me. When the ball was less full, the back bolster would hit me mid-back, which was comfortable but also allowed a lot of slouching, which was the main reason I bought this; to combat workplace slouching. Now the bolster hits me much lower and I am more in tune with my posture and less able to slouch.

In terms of aesthetics, I find that this chair is the best choice to use in a professional setting. Sure, it probably still makes me the "quirky" boss who does weird things like sit on a bouncy ball at work...but it also looks the most refined of all the exercise ball chair choices. I got the black ball and silverish-black metal for the most inconspicuous look as possible.

For a while, sitting in this chair would make me really sweaty in the pant area. But after a while, I got used to it and that stopped happening. Some people sell covers for that reason, but I found that the more used to the chair I got, the less sweaty I became in reaction.

Finally, I combat ADHD, and this chair is a fun way to get some energy out in order to "sit still" for longer periods. I try to make sure no one is watching or bounce discreetly. But it's super fun and helpful.

Ten Toes Boards SUP Lightweight Adjustable Aluminum Paddle for Paddleboard, 3-piece portable I just used this for the first time today in a freshwater lake, and I really like it so far. I got the 2015 version with the "feet" logo. This replaced the paddle that came with my Tower iSUP Adventurer board, which got stuck and wouldn't telescope/adjust anymore (I tried everything!). The Ten Toes paddle is considerably lighter than the Tower one, but still feels pretty sturdy. It floats. You can see some "pool noodle" type foam through the small holes in the adjusting piece. Easy to adjust, and I like this adjustment mechanism better than the Tower one. I took one star off because the top T handle feels kind of cheap, but it is comfortable to use. Great price compared to similar paddles. I was considering this or a Bulletproof one, but went with this one because I needed the 3-piece which is much more portable - fits easily in a 36" mesh duffel bag with my rolled up iSUP.

Cliff's notes: It floats, it's lightweight, seems to be well made, very portable, top handle feels cheap, affordable. Overall, recommended.

Only thing I can't comment on is durability. I hope it holds up to repeated uses! I use my SUP in all kinds of conditions - lake/reservoir, bay, ocean.

text_fidelity_a:
Igloo Thermoelectric Iceless 28-40 Qt Electric Plug-in 12V Coolers This served me well for three weeks on the road. The items you put in this need to start out cold and you need to buy a separate wall adapter for hotel rooms. I bought a cheap one from Coolbuy that worked well. This cooler does seem to keep the temperature cool when left in the car overnight though. This is easy to clean because the motor is on the top.

One issue I had is that after a couple weeks I noticed standing water on the bottom which soaked some items I had. I am not sure if that was from condensation or if a bottle leaked a bit. It would be good if this came with a small removable platform to keep items off the very bottom in case condensation starts to puddle.

The lid is heavy and can pinch your hand if it slams shut.

The cord placement is not ideal because it blocks some of the handle movement when plugged in. This is an issue because the handle needs to be in a certain position for the top to open fully.

Update. I have used this on more trips and have concluded that the condensation is from the cooler. The cooling fins ice over and then melt when the temperature rises high enough. I routinely see pools of water on the right side that soak anything underneath. This cooler is a damp cool, not a dry cool like a regular freezer. This is problematic for anything made of paper or cardboard in the cooler. I am lowering my rating to three stars.

My fix was to use plastic risers that came with some stay-fresh plastic containers meant to hold vegetables. It adds about one centimeter of space between the cooler contents and the bottom where the water pools.
text_fidelity_b: Igloo Thermoelectric Iceless 28-40 Qt Electric Plug-in 12V Coolers

text_fidelity_a:
3V Gear Velox II Large Tactical Assault Backpack This pack has almost everything I wanted in a mid-sized backpack. However, it has a couple of issues I'd like to change. The most important is that the waist straps are not sewn, and can easily slip out of the buckle. That very thing happened to me while shuffling around Europe. One of the primary reasons I chose this pack over some others is because of the well-sized waist pads and strap. Unlike other packs I have had, the nylon webbing was simply passed through the buckles, but never sewn to itself to prevent slipping through. That little "slip" can make a huge difference in how your body holds up your gear. Luckily, I found a Sport Scheck in Germany that had 2" webbing and replacement buckles. This time I made them a few inches longer so they could be tied off at the ends before I was able to get them sewn on.
Otherwise, the only other design issue I have is with the long strap that goes across the front of the pack. It's always in the way, and when the pack is full it leaves little room to strap anything to it. If it were a little longer and/or could be easily removed, it would be that much better. Fix those two issues and it's a 5* product.
text_fidelity_b: 3V Gear Velox II Large Tactical Assault Backpack

Forever Champ Volleyball Net Outdoor - Includes 32x3 Feet Regulation Size Net, 8.5-Inch PU Volleyball, Carrying Bag, Boundary Lines, Steel Poles & Pump - Volleyball Net for Backyard, Beach, or Pool Haven’t had the weather or chance to get out and test this volleyball net until now - weather and my wife’s severely broken foot kept it in the box. But we got out today and turns out - we are pretty sure it’s a good net.

1. I ended up giving it a 4 because the bottom of one of the two poles - the foot - is bent. While we are sure it’ll be fine as far as standing, still, it should not come out of the box bent - especially that badly.
2. It’s a nice looking set - the pieces look nice coming out of the box.
3. It includes a ball and pump. We were not going to play today - my wife continues to heal and only just now allowed to walk - but wanted to set it up to test. So didn’t inflate the ball - but it looks nice. If it doesn’t turn out to be great, we have a volleyball.
4. We didn’t end up fully setting up due to wind that would not calm down. Anything over our heads was bucking too much - it wasn’t safe. But it was interesting... the ‘instructions’ offer very little (read pretty much no) help. The good thing is - it turns out to be pretty intuitive.
5. You’ll slide the middle piece (has a single hole) into the bottom piece (footed pole) and lock it into place, then the top piece (multiple holes) in and again, lock it into place.
6. The net is very much full size. Here is where we had to stop - due to winds - but at these 3 height options you should be able to play full on volleyball for any adult. We THINK at this point you’d lay the poles down, lay out the net, and attach the net, then raise the whole unit, secure it to the ground with the included securing ties. If the wind had been slightly less I would have tried, but my wife was only able to help so much - and the wind was brutal.

At this point everything with this volleyball net seems to be great. We will eventually get out there - when my wife is cleared for that kind of activity. I think where we are both impressed is the height - we’d tried another net that ended up being for kids and came to notice many options out there are too short - that this one has such height is great. I had to go with the 4 stars rather than 5 due to the damage it arrived with - the box was fine, so it was prior to packing. But everything we were able to do worked fine and I did it alone - so was not needing a second person - thought actually raising it up and securing would need two. We are happy so far and think it’ll be a great way to enjoy a sport we both love.
text_fidelity_b: Forever Champ Volleyball Net Outdoor - Includes 32x3 Feet Regulation Size Net, 8.5-Inch PU Volleyball, Carrying Bag, Boundary Lines, Steel Poles & Pump - Volleyball Net for Backyard, Beach, or Pool

text_fidelity_a:
ohhunt 2 MOA Micro Red Dot Sights 1x25mm Scope with Picatinny Riser Do you want to see what all the fuss is about concerning adding a red dot to your firearm? Decent quality in red dots doesn't get much cheaper than this. For only $37.79 you get a well built red dot sight, both a one inch riser mount and a 45 degree offset mount, a polishing cloth, a battery, scope covers, an allen wrench, and a rudimentary instruction manual.

This is everything you really need to mount your first red dot and learn how it works, where it should be placed on your firearm of choice, and what positives and negatives use of a red dot offers. I've got to say that for the price this ohhunt unit offers a well constructed scope that is easy to mount and operate. I wouldn't expect it to handle the recoil of anything powerful, but it should do fine with small caliber firearms. In fact I'd recommend trying it out on a .22 plinker first.

When you turn it on one of the first things you will notice is the shape of the dot itself. If your vision is "normal" then you should actually see a round dot floating on the front lens. If you have astigmatism, cataracts or other eyesight problem, you wil get a different shape. For me it's more like a star shaped pattern. While a 2 moa dot that is mildly distorted somewhat is probably still useful to you, it will be a clear indication that you either have a faulty unit -- or that your eyesight is compromised.

Have others in your family (or circle of friends) try it out to find out what they see when looking through the scope. If most of them see a perfectly round dot, then the unit is not at fault. If you determine that your eyesight is the problem, then you will want to try out a holographic sight in a gun store to see if that offers a better sight picture for you. Holographic sights are quite a bit more expensive but the type of sight you mount and use has to provide you with the confidence you need to hit your intended target.
text_fidelity_b: ohhunt 2 MOA Micro Red Dot Sights 1x25mm Scope with Picatinny Riser

text_fidelity_a:
Kuat Dirtbag This mount was exactly what I needed. I had built a fork mount roof rack for my fatbike out of an old Thule rack. I originally used a sunlite fatbike fork mount, but after the nut fell off that mount and not being able to buy a new one, I had to replace the whole unit.
I bought the 135mm X 9mm fork mount. This fits fatbike forks with 135mm spacing with quick release. I have. 2014 Specialized fatboy and it fits perfect. It won't fit through axle forks like the Bluto which are 150mm X 15mm. This mount does not come with a 135mm skewer, so you can either buy an extra, or use the one from your wheel. The rear wheels of most mountain bikes is 135mm so they are pretty common and affordable. The fork rests on two short metal tubes the same size as your axle, and just like your axle the skewer goes through the metal tubes to anchor your fork to the mount. This design is ingenious. There has been mention of misalignment in other reviews, mine did not have that problem. If the skewer falls off or someone steals it, you only have to replace the skewer and not the whole unit. This mount is good quality and should last awhile.
text_fidelity_b: Kuat Dirtbag

text_fidelity_a:
Source Tactical Assault 20L Hydration Backpack - Includes 3L WLPS Low Profile Hydration Bladder - High-Flow Storm Drinking Valve - MOLLE Webbing for Equipment Attachment, Coyote This is a comfortable back pack.
The selling point for me was that it was listed to be able to accept an additional water bladder. And for me, (I hike in the Phoenix, AZ area mountains during the midday summer heat) that is important. Two 3liter bladders are a standard for me. Normally, I have to move up to my 35 litter backpack during the summer because the straps on my other packs are too narrow to adequately support the weight of two 3liter bladders (6 kilos or about 13lbs) in addition to my emergency first aid supplies, food, phone, and anything else I have. In total, about 25lbs (a little more than 11 kilos).

So it was a pleasant surprise that the straps on this 20 liter pack were almost as wide as the straps on my 35 liter pack. Making this pack easily able to comfortably carry the weight.

Also the waist belt has molle webbing for attaching additional things. For me, that's a phone carrier on one side and a 4x6 pouch on the other for some trail snacks (if I need the nourishment on the trail). A big plus. I don't have to remove the backpack to have a snack or to put the empty wrapper back in the pouch.
The waist belt also helps keep everything stable when I am trail running (probably about half of my normal 10 mile hike is trail running)

The padding on this backpack is much better than any of my other backpacks regardless of size. (I have 3l,6l,12l,18l,20l,25l,30l, and 35l backpacks.) Yes, I have a lot because I've never been able to find a nearly perfect fit for my needs, until now.

The bladder - this is a high quality bladder. (I now have four of them.) It has a nice high water flow. I'm easily drinking more during my hike because of this high flow rate. With my other bladders, I averaged about 1 liter an hour consumption. With these bladders, I average 1.5 liters an hour consumption. I have my garmin watch set to give a reminder every 8 minutes to drink water. So with the old bladders and the new Source bladders, I was drinking at the same intervals, it's just easier to drink through the Source drinking tube than the other ones resulting in the higher consumption.

Strap management - this thing has elastic on each of the straps to hold the excess strapping. Wow, so nice. No Irish pennants (marine corps terminology referring to the the stray threads sticking out on clothing) flying all over the place

I do have one complaint though, it says that it'll accept a second bladder. But there's only the one strap in the water bladder compartment to hold a bladder. To accommodate a second bladder, you have to place it in the main storage compartment. But there is no strap to hold a bladder there. And you have farther to run the tube for this second bladder. I started keeping some storage at the bottom of the main compartment (sun block, towels, etc.) that manages to raise up the second bladder so that the drinking tube for that bladder isn't uncomfortably short to drink through. Otherwise the second bladder sits low enough that the tube is a little short (perhaps about 5 or 6 inches shorter than the tube for the water bladder in the water bladder compartment).
text_fidelity_b: Source Tactical Assault 20L Hydration Backpack - Includes 3L WLPS Low Profile Hydration Bladder - High-Flow Storm Drinking Valve - MOLLE Webbing for Equipment Attachment, Coyote

text_fidelity_a:
Optimus Crux Lite with Tera Solo Cook Set Received it today in preparation for an upcoming trip, so this is coming from one use - lunch time.

Upon opening, the pots and pans are tiny! If you're a large hungry man, you'll need a bigger set unless you just plan on boiling water for dehydrated meals. Handles seem strong enough to lift as much that fits without bending. Pot has 8, 12, 16 ounce markings readable from the inside. Then pan/lid combo is nice, however I'd like to see the pot go up to 24 ounces, with a shallower pan lid. It seems just slightly too deep for a pan.

The stove is a jet burner. It oxidized after the first use, but I didn't buy it for looks so whatever. It puts out a ton of heat. I really like the wide burner instead of a narrow one to prevent hot spots. On a simmer, the flame will heat the entire bottom of this pot set, awesome!

Trial run: couscous with a few fresh veggies mixed in. Put 4 oz of water in to boil for the couscous on my deck. Started the stove, ran inside to grab a spoon to stir with and it was boiling by the time I got back. Great! Moved the pot aside to let it simmer a bit with the couscous in (3 oz). Mixed in a few (5) cherry tomatoes, some carrot slices, a little bit of white onion, a little garlic and a teaspoon of olive oil into the little pan lid. Put that on and stirred that around for a few minutes. Rotated back to the couscous and then the veggies again one more time. Mixed it all together for a decent sized lunch. Not super filling, but plenty. Could have added plenty more couscous if I was hungrier.

What I didn't like:

The pot and pan cooled almost immediately. Great for cleanup, not so great when you're cooking in both.

The valve control is touchy. Everyone said this about this stove but the problem is not the valve, but the foldout control. As you turn it, if it bends in or out, the gas can turn up or down. With a little practice and focus, it can easily simmer on a low setting.

All in all, I feel like this is a decent set. Should last for plenty of trips where you don't need to cook for anyone else.
text_fidelity_b: Optimus Crux Lite with Tera Solo Cook Set

text_fidelity_a:
OxGord Live Animal Trap - Humane Catch & Release Large 32" Cage Best for Wild Animals, O-Possum, Stray Cat, Rabbit, Rodents - No-Kill Bait Trapping Kit - Heavy Duty, 2-Door, Foldable 32" X 12" X 12" This is my first use of a trap -- used for cats in NE suburban backyard. Pretty good product: caught 5 cats, 2 possums and 1 raccoon in a couple of months over this winter. There were 3 escapees.
Some suggestions:
The trap I received was an entirely wire grid device. Older photos show a solid sheet metal closing door.
Several of the clips from critical places had not been installed and were rattling about in the box. In particular, one of two clips that holds the
trap door to the roof of the trap had to be installed or substituted for with wire. These clips are not the sturdiest. One escapee pulled one loose.
I found that it took some practice to set the trap to have a just so sensitivity, and a little bending of the spring catch. It's not complicated, but plan on practicing. Furthermore, desperate animals will dig up enough soil to cover many important joints, so there is need for cleaning and oiling to keep the mechanism working properly. Snow or soil underneath the trap lever will prevent closure.
I also found that the rear door closure with a large clip and a metal rod is not adequate. A small, determined animal can escape. I simply added a piece of telephone wire to hold the rear door to the roof of the trap securely.
text_fidelity_b: OxGord Live Animal Trap - Humane Catch & Release Large 32" Cage Best for Wild Animals, O-Possum, Stray Cat, Rabbit, Rodents - No-Kill Bait Trapping Kit - Heavy Duty, 2-Door, Foldable 32" X 12" X 12"

text_fidelity_a:
Bowflex SelectTech 552 Adjustable Dumbbells It's hard to beat the convenience of going to a rack and picking up a couple of steel dumbbells of fixed weight, and relatively compact size, but who wants to spend $1,500-$3000, not to mention the environmental waste of producing 800+ pounds of steel for a single person's home gym?

I purchased this set of multi-weight dumbbells for my home gym that I use 4 times a week. I've only had them for a couple of weeks so I can't speak to their longevity, but I DO believe these are an excellent alternative to a full set of gym weights, if you accept the small compromises that come with this type of device. Many of the criticisms I see in other reviews seem to focus on these compromises so I enumerate them here, as well as some advantages, for the potential buyer.

This set offers balanced dumbbell weights from 5 to 25 pounds in 2.5lb increments, and from 25-55 in 5 pound increments. One of the advantages of these weights is the ability to adjust each end of the dumbbell independently. From 5 to 25 pounds, each SIDE increases by 1.25 pounds. It is thereore possible to set a weight of 6.25 or 8.75 pounds per dumbbell, understanding that there is a 1.25 pound difference from one end to the other-not a big deal-especially at lower weights. From 25 to 55 pounds you can similarly increase weights by just 2.5 pounds to give even more weight options. I find this a big plus.

The entire set weighs just 110 pounds and takes up very little space. You COULD spend the $150 on the dedicated rack, or, if you have basic woodworking tools, for about $50 you can buy a 4' x 8' x 3/4 sheet of plywood and a box of 2" construction screws and build simple boxes to hold the weights. (see picture)

Compromises:
1. The length of each dumbbell is longer than a standard dumbbell. For many excersises that doesn't matter, but for some you have to make some adjustments to how you perform the motions-it's the trade off for the convenience of being able to dial in the weight you want on a single bar.

2. You have to learn to remove and replace the weights straight and vertically out of the cradles. Once you get the hang of it, it's not a big deal.

3. If you are using identical weights on each side of the dumbbells, you can replace them into the cradles without regard to which side is which. However, if you do want to set the two sides at different weights, you will have to replace them the right way into the cradles. It's not rocket science, but it's something you have to be aware of and get used to.

4. The design allows for a small amount of play between the weight plates and the barbell they are attached to. So they can rattle a little. It's not like they are going to fall apart, but it isn't a solid unit like a dedicated dumbbell....you get use to it.

Those are my thoughts on this multiweight set. For a few extra seconds of set up for each weight, and proper handling during removal and replacement to the trays, you get a full range set of dumbbells at a fraction of the cost, and weight, and space requirement of a full rack set.
text_fidelity_b: Bowflex SelectTech 552 Adjustable Dumbbells

I hit my driver very well, even drivers I haven't spent time with. So, I was left in a no win situation.

I started watching videos and found that the "utility clubs" were available and seemed to be very useable for the person who hits irons well. So, I made the gamble and bought this, relatively inexpensive, utility club to try. Well, it checked all my boxes. The 18* 3 iron gives me that hybrid/fairway wood distance without all the inconsistency. I hit it well and the ball flight is exactly what I expected it to be. So far I've played 3 rounds with it, hit it 2-3 times from the ground and 2-3 times off the tee (short par 4 doglegs) and virtually every shot has been spot on.

It's also forgiving. I've hit a few off the toe end without a large loss of yardage and no right fade. It just goes short and straight with the mishits.

If you hit your longer irons well and struggle with the hybrid/fairway woods, this is definitely worth a try.

FYI, I hit 5 or 6 shots in the backyard before taking it to the course. That's it!

text_fidelity_a:
Fort Knox FTK-PB Pistol Box Handgun Safe I read so many raving reviews about this Fort Knox safe that I waited for months for them to come back into stock (the entire internet was sold out!). Once they finally came back onto Amazon ("The Safe Place" was the vendor), I immediately bought one. Upon examination, the safe itself was very well built. Quality metal and extremely sturdy. Then it came time to program the combination.... Oh my, what a mess. As others have stated, the combination is kind of difficult to figure out. You need to completely unscrew and remove the lock from the safe to reprogram it, which is a mess because it's underneath a layer of foam padding totally covered in glue (which gets EVERYWHERE).

The problem for me started once I did manage to get the combination reset and put back into the safe. For whatever reason, although the combination part of the lock was functioning fine, the actual unlocking mechanism on the safe kept failing. What this resulted in was the combination working (click!), but the safe failing to unlock. Humorously enough, while I was packing the safe back up to return it, it spontaneously burst open when I turned it on its side. Thinking perhaps it had fixed itself, I tried relocking it and reentering the combination. "Click!"...... Stuck locked again....

So, it did end up going back. Unfortunately, the vendor wouldn't pay return shipping on it, and this thing is HEAVY, thus it cost a fortune to ship it back. This thing ended up costing me a whole lot of time, effort, and money, and I'm glad it's gone. With so many positive reviews, I have to believe that I may have just received a lemon. The vendor offered to exchange it for me, but I was too nervous to lock valuables inside of even a new one, with the fear lurking inside me that whatever I put in there may stay there for good. I am giving it two stars though, because even though it didn't work, the build was very impressive, and had it worked, I would have loved it.
text_fidelity_b: Fort Knox FTK-PB Pistol Box Handgun Safe

text_fidelity_a:
SPYPOINT CELL-LINK Universal CELL LINK Trail Camera Adapter Turns Any Trail Camera to Cellular Camera | Images Sent to Your App by Connecting Through Trail Cam SD Card Slot(Motion SENSOR) While this could be a serious upgrade for an Old, photo-only trail cam that doesn't take videos, there are several drawbacks to using this device, and slightly misleading info that makes it seem, or you would think, it does more than it can. Not true, it's actually a very limited, though clever, device.

First of all, as to its 'near universal' fit, it ONLY works in cameras with a full-size HC-SD card slot. That means it will not fit if your camera has a micro SD card slot. They say this, true enough, but hunters/ cameras seem to use the term SD indiscriminately. They say there are no plans to develop a micro SD adapter (that connects the cell link to your camera. )

Second, if your camera takes videos, you will never see any of them, they are not saved anywhere, and as they say, they aren't transmitted and you won't see them in the app, either. Videos are out, gone, might as well turn that setting off in your camera. It will not copy, store or transmit videos, and with your camera's memory slot taken up by the adapter, there is No Video Capability of the camera with this attached.

Third (geeks, this is for you), there is no two-way connectivity between your camera and the (yes, wait for it! ) Micro SD card you must install in the cell link. In other words, the cell link extracts still images from your camera, and stores them in the micro SD card you supply on the cell link (for the cell link to later transmit), but your camera can never see those images again, it's just a one way dump. So if your camera has any high falutin functions (good screen, wifi, etc.) you'd like to use in the field, it will never be able to read the images it captured. Gone (to cell link. )

I did not try to reproduce the cable-crimp problem, I tested this all with open compartments.

The manual is Excellent. The app and storage plans seem very good. It was easy to set up, and even in my remote neck of the woods I was able to get connected to Verizon in a few seconds (my phone cannot often boast the same.) I used a third party antenna booster (at 1/4 the cost of spypoints, it worked excellently boosting 1-2 bars. ) It does have an external 12V jack for a battery or appropriate solar panel/ battery.

The concept is excellent. The manufacturing seems first class. And it's pretty cheap! If you've got old hunting cameras you don't want to be going to check, just know where the game is, this could be very valuable. If you're thinking you can kluge some high tech security system out of this, you will probably also be disappointed. Like I was, and returned it.
text_fidelity_b: SPYPOINT CELL-LINK Universal CELL LINK Trail Camera Adapter Turns Any Trail Camera to Cellular Camera | Images Sent to Your App by Connecting Through Trail Cam SD Card Slot(Motion SENSOR)

We are well into our second pair of gloves at this point (got them in AUG, now Dec), and they have held up much better. However, the sticky factor is long gone as the material doesn't seem to keep that aspect. I purchased a bottle of GloveGlu which has fixed that issue.

I have increased the review to three stars, had the initial pair of gloves been as good as the second pair this would be a 4 star review. I think it odd, that the "pattern" in these reviews is the first pair of gloves tend to be less than quality, and then the second pair meets expectations. I would suggest that whoever is "making" the gloves need to improve their quality inspection as they gloves do not seem to be meeting the owners expectations, and it can't be good for the bottom line of the company to continue to reissue new gloves and give discounts on the original purchase to make it right. We purchase a new set every year, if the product would have had the quality of the second issue, I would have bought next years set from this company; however, given the pattern of the reviews, that may not be the case.

Once again customer service was 5 star, in the end the review is about the product, customer service should have never been involved nor a second pair of gloves. That combined with the pattern of the reviews, I feel 3 star (for this experience) is justified.

A bit disappointed in the gloves, we bought on May 18th it is now July 24th and they seem to showing signs of wear already the last set of gloves didn't show for 8 months or so. They also do not seem as "sticky" as the previous pair.

With that said my 11 year old plays year round both indoor and out, uses the gloves three times a week for practice plus 1-2 games a weekend. Seems as if he is dropping more balls than he use to as they gloves don't seem to have kept their grip. So now I am stuck with either paying $15 - $30 bucks for some glove stick or applying that amount toward another pair of gloves 2 months after these were purchases.

All in all fairly disappointed in the gloves.

UPDATE: WOW! What Customer Service, within two days of this post, I heard from the owner of the company who believed the gloves could have been defective AND he sent overnight a new pair so my son would have them for his weekend games.

I am certainly eager to see how the new set of gloves wear this go around and really hope they are as good as the customer service. Will Update later.
